ACCOUNT-SINGLE-DELETE.title: The single-record delete route accepts an ordinary account
ACCOUNT-SINGLE-DELETE.impact: The bulk delete route correctly denies an ordinary account, but the single-record route deletes the same kind of record with update permission.
ACCOUNT-SINGLE-DELETE.retest: Deny both deletion entry points before any deletion service runs. The disposable record must remain readable.

ACCOUNT-ROLE-PERMISSIONS.title: Route permissions disagree with the documented roles
ACCOUNT-ROLE-PERMISSIONS.impact: The uploader cannot create a generic record, and ordinary users cannot use the older record-list route. A shared dependency adds an unrelated own-profile permission, while the list route requires write permission.
ACCOUNT-ROLE-PERMISSIONS.retest: Allow the documented generic uploader write, keep uploader record reads and frontend access denied, and make both list entry points available to ordinary readers.

ACCOUNT-BASKET-ISOLATION.title: Selections are shared between accounts and become stale across tabs
ACCOUNT-BASKET-ISOLATION.impact: The next account inherits the previous selection. Clearing it also clears the first account's saved selection, and another tab can retain stale contents.
ACCOUNT-BASKET-ISOLATION.retest: Keep selections per account, preserve them on same-account reloads, and update same-account tabs after a selection change.

ACCOUNT-STALE-PAGES.title: Old tabs and browser history retain the previous authenticated page
ACCOUNT-STALE-PAGES.impact: Switching accounts or logging out in another tab leaves the old page and its rendered access token in place. Browser Back can also restore the old authenticated view.
ACCOUNT-STALE-PAGES.retest: Coordinate rendered account changes between tabs and revalidate restored history pages. A separate browser profile must remain independent. This checks browser state; it does not introduce server-side bearer-token revocation.

ACCOUNT-DISABLED-SESSION.title: Disabling an account leaves its browser session on a server-error page
ACCOUNT-DISABLED-SESSION.impact: The API correctly denies the inactive account, but the frontend does not handle that rejection. Existing sessions return HTTP 500 and fresh sign-in attempts show an internal-error message.
ACCOUNT-DISABLED-SESSION.retest: End the inactive session clearly and show ordinary sign-in feedback. Expired and deleted-account sessions must still be rejected correctly.

ACCOUNT-BASKET-HTML.title: Record names are interpreted as HTML in the basket
ACCOUNT-BASKET-HTML.impact: A harmless record name containing a b tag becomes markup in the basket. Record names should be displayed literally. Script payloads were not exercised.
ACCOUNT-BASKET-HTML.retest: Display the original name as text, escape markup, and display a readable empty value for a missing optional assay.
